environment.user: root (the distro has no other user); session bus at /run/user/0/bus
environment.caveat: WSLg rendering is software/virtualised (llvmpipe). Absolute times and especially RSS of GPU-renderer toolkits (GL/Vulkan/wgpu) are inflated by Mesa llvmpipe (~100+ MB, one worker thread per core). Compare numbers relative to each other, not to a real desktop. 'Cold' = after echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches inside WSL; the Windows host may still cache the ext4.vhdx, so cold is only partially cold.

method.startup: launchwait.c: fork/exec, poll the X11 window tree every 2 ms until a window with the probe title is IsViewable (mapped). Run under X11 with WAYLAND_DISPLAY unset, GDK_BACKEND=x11, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb. 1 cold run then 3 warm runs, process group killed between runs. tray-only has no window: time to its 'ready' stdout line after tray icon + hotkey registration.
method.memory: last warm run, after 10 s idle: Rss and Pss from /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup, Threads from /proc/<pid>/status.
method.runtime_libs: shared objects mapped in /proc/<pid>/maps at the memory sample (includes dlopen'ed libraries that ldd does not show), mapped to Debian packages with dpkg -S.
method.wayland: wayland-check.sh: DISPLAY unset, WAYLAND_DEBUG=client, GDK_BACKEND=wayland, QT_QPA_PLATFORM=wayland; ok = alive after 5 s and created an xdg_toplevel. Does not prove correct rendering.
method.notification_daemon: Installing the probes' deps pulled in dunst, whose D-Bus-activated systemd unit crashes in WSL (no DISPLAY) and makes org.freedesktop.Notifications activation hang ~25 s. Eto.Gtk calls libnotify at startup and measured 22-28 s because of this. For the final pass dunst was started manually with DISPLAY=:0 so a notification server answers, as on a real desktop.
method.size: shipped_bytes = everything that must be distributed (binary + bundled native libs; .pdb/.dbg excluded). targz_bytes = tar.gz -9 of that directory.
